description: The pull-up is the one test where bodyweight is both the exam and the equipment. Your number exposes the lat and elbow tendons that carry every rep, and it is the test where the skinny build stops apologizing. Today you get your number, the science under it, and the thirty-day plan.

lines: It is also a starting line.
beats.title: EVERY REP FROM STRAIGHT ARMS

scenes.narration: Grab the bar. | Hang at the bottom. | Arms fully straight. | Now pull up. | Chin over the bar. | Lower back down. | All the way down. | Count clean reps only. | No kicking allowed. | No half reps. | Stop when form breaks. | That number is yours. | Write it down. | Zero is allowed. | Zero is data. | Here is the secret. | This lift is decided | by tendons again. | Lat cables below. | Elbow cables above. | At the end today | I show you why. | Keep your number.

scenes.label: THE LINE BETWEEN CLIMBING AND OWNING
scenes.narration: Here is the line. Ten strict pull-ups is where climbing the bar becomes owning the bar. Zero to two reps is the most crowded category on earth, and it is a starting line, not a sentence. Three to nine means the chain works and needs volume. Over fifteen strict reps puts you in rare relative-strength territory, where your bodyweight has become a light load. Whatever your number was, hold it next to that line. This test is famous for humbling big physiques, and by the end of this video you will know exactly which tissues do the humbling. And if your number today is zero, understand that zero pull-ups with strong potential is the single most common starting point among people who later do twenty.
scenes.sub: 0-2 reps: the normal start - over 15: relative strength elite

beats.text: THE BOTTOM IS A LOADED STRETCH
THE CHAIN IS THE MUSCLE'S BOSS

scenes.narration: A pull-up is two cable systems working in relay. Your lats, the big wings of your back, do not grip your arm bone directly. Their force travels through the lat tendon into the upper arm, hauling it down and back. At the same time, your elbow flexors bend the arm, and their force travels through the biceps tendon and its partners across the elbow joint. Every single rep sends your entire bodyweight through both systems at once. Now look at the bottom of the rep, the dead hang position where strict form begins. There, your arms are straight, your shoulders are stretched overhead, and the tendons of both systems sit under full load at full length. That loaded stretch is the most tendon-intensive moment in the whole lift, and it is the moment sloppy form deletes. A chain, as the saying goes, is graded by its links, and in the pull-up the links are not muscles. The muscles are strong in almost everyone who trains. The links, the lat insertion and the elbow tendons, decide how much of that strength ever becomes a rep. The scapula, your shoulder blade, is the chain's foundation stone. Before your arms bend, the muscles that pull your shoulder blades down must set them like anchors, and their tendons take the first share of every rep's load. A pull-up that starts with a shrug is a chain that starts with a loose first link. This is why the dead hang you met earlier in this series is secretly pull-up training: it builds the anchor position the whole lift stands on.

This is why strict reps build what kipping never will. A kip uses hip momentum to throw the body upward, and momentum is a loan. It pays part of the bill so the tendons do not have to, which means the tissues that limit your pull-up receive a smaller training signal from a bigger-looking performance. Strict reps are the opposite bargain. Every inch is funded by muscle through tendon, with a long, honest pause of tension at the stretched bottom. Tendons adapt to exactly that: high tension, held and repeated. The negative, the lowering half, is the other half of the medicine. Lowering under control is eccentric loading, the style of tension tendon research keeps returning to because it organizes collagen along the line of stress. A pull-up program built on strict reps and slow negatives is secretly a tendon program wearing a strength costume. Your number at the start of this video was limited by those tissues. Train them directly and the number has no choice but to follow. Tempo is the final variable. A pull-up lowered in one second and a pull-up lowered in four are different exercises wearing the same name. The slow one delivers roughly four times the tendon tension-time per rep, which is why disciplined negatives build people who cannot yet do a single full rep.

beats.text: BIG GUYS LIFT MORE PER REP

scenes.narration: Now the advantage, and no test in this series favors you like this one. A pull-up moves your body and nothing else, so the score is pure relative strength: force produced per kilo carried. The heavy lifter's muscles are bigger in absolute terms, but his tendons are not proportionally bigger, and every rep asks those similar-sized cables to haul far more cargo. Your cables haul less. That is why the world records and the freakish rep counts in this lift belong overwhelmingly to light, wiry athletes. It is also why a skinny beginner can go from zero to ten in a season while a much stronger-on-paper heavy trainee fights for five. His ceiling is taxed by his own mass. Yours is not. Understand what this means practically. The pull-up is the rare arena where the thing the world told you was your weakness, being light, functions as equipment. You are not compensating here. You are specialized. Every other test in this series gives you an edge. This one gives you the home stadium, the home crowd, and the lighter bar. All that is left is to train the chain.
Train with me. Four rounds of thirty seconds of pull-up work, singles or slow negatives, with a full minute of rest. Every rep from straight arms, every lowering slow. Go.

Your plan, and the three cheats that keep pull-up numbers at two forever. Cheat one is the kip, swinging your way up and calling it a rep. Cheat two is the half lowering, dropping only until your elbows bend slightly, which deletes the loaded stretch where the tendon training lives. Cheat three is the almost rep, chin hovering under the bar while the set gets counted anyway. If the chin does not clear, the rep does not exist. The method that actually builds this lift is famous among gymnasts and soldiers. Grease the groove. Many times a day, do one or two perfect reps, far from failure, and walk away. Singles in the morning, singles after lunch, singles whenever you pass the bar. The chain learns the pattern, the tendons collect tension time without exhaustion, and your max climbs as a side effect. Once a week, test honestly. The rest of the week, practice like it is a skill, because it is one.

scenes.label: RETEST - SAME BAR, STRICT RULES
scenes.narration: So, your number. Zero to two: the normal human start, and in this lift the fastest-improving category there is. Three to nine: the chain is awake and asking for volume, which the daily singles will happily provide. Ten to fifteen: you own the bar, moving your body like it is light, because for you it is. Over fifteen: relative-strength elite, a number most people never touch at any size. Write your number in the comments. Just the number. In thirty days we return to the same bar under the same strict rules, and the chain will report its own progress.
scenes.sub: comment your number below - then beat it

scenes.narration: Thirty days from now, the same bar and a number that tells the truth about your chain. Subscribe for the retest and for the next test in this series. This is {channel}. Train the cable.
